title: ready-01: heca as a library, with an entry point for adding things
summary: The heca crate becomes library + small main.rs; another crate can add actions, docks, pane decorations and overlays at startup.
description:
heca-pro uses heca's crates as Cargo git dependencies (decision 1 in `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/decisions.md`). For that, the `heca` crate must also be a library.

## Current state
- `heca/Cargo.toml:2` — program only, no `[lib]`.
- `HecaApp` (private) in `heca/src/main.rs:50`; `fn main` at :475; app setup in `heca/src/app/startup.rs`.
- Actions are registered in the ActionCatalog (`heca/src/actions/`); docks come from providers (`heca/src/providers/`, e.g. the workspaces dock); overlays/layers from `heca/src/chrome/`.

## Goal
- `heca/src/lib.rs` exposes the app; `main.rs` shrinks to a few lines calling it. **The `heca` program builds and runs exactly as today.**
- One public entry point (a builder on the app) where another crate adds, before the app starts: actions, docks (providers), pane decorations, overlays. Write it as the line a plugin author would type — no registry ids, no crate-private types. It is the same opening the plugin system needs; reuse the provider/ActionCatalog paths, never a second one.
- heca-pro can then depend on heca pinned to a tag/commit, with a local path override for working on both.

## Preserve
- Every current behaviour of the `heca` binary; all tests green.
- AGENTS.md § 0/0b/0d; no hard-coded placement — a heca-pro dock is placed by the user like any dock.

## Done when
- A tiny example crate (or test) builds an app through the entry point, adds one action and one dock, and both work (action reachable by key, menu and RPC; dock placeable in either sidebar).

tasks.title: Split heca into library + program, and add the entry point another crate uses to add actions, docks, pane decorations and overlays
tasks.description:
Execution task for P098. Read the phase description first, and `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/architecture.md` ("Two editions, one code base underneath").

Current: `heca/Cargo.toml:2` program only; `HecaApp` private at `heca/src/main.rs:50`; `fn main` at :475; startup in `heca/src/app/startup.rs`; actions in the ActionCatalog (`heca/src/actions/`); docks from providers (`heca/src/providers/`).

Steps are in the checklist. Design the entry point first and agree it with Antonio before writing it (it is a public API a plugin author will also read) — write the line a plugin author would type. Edge cases: the binary must not change behaviour; tests that reach private items keep working; nothing heca-pro adds may need a registry id.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-09-30 (code and docs uncommitted in worktree ~/projects/heca-f012, branch feat/f012-heca-library on origin/main 6666fdc4; PR to follow). SHIPPED: (1) heca is a library + one-line main.rs: `heca::run()` (heca/src/lib.rs, main.rs). (2) The doors another crate uses, heca/src/entry/: `heca::extension("pro")` (name declared once; `heca` reserved; dotted/empty/duplicate refused and reported) and, off the handle, `pro.action(..)` (server side; ActionMeta builders, handler gets ProviderCx), `pro.layer(..)` (client side; named layer opened with toggle_layer; built again each open), `pro.pane_button(..)`, `pro.pane_chip(..)`, `pro.pane_line(..)`; docks use the existing public `heca::regions(..).append(..)` with the Provider types made public. (3) Pane decoration by name: heca/src/chrome/pane_items/{buttons,chips,lines,listing}.rs; the closed PaneAction/PaneSegment enums are gone; `[appearance.pane] title_actions`, `title_segments` and new `[appearance.sidebar] pane_lines` list items by name with today's spellings; heca's own items (six buttons, five chips, cwd and git lines in providers/workspaces/row_lines.rs) are registered through the same defs an extension uses; the three listing rules (user's list is the list; extension items show only while the list is the default; an omitted added item is announced once via announced.json) are written once in listing.rs; PaneFacts/PaneChip/PaneLine are non_exhaustive; an added chip re-runs only when its pane's facts change. (4) Folder-line decision (Antonio): sidebar lines decided by pane_lines alone (default cwd+git); `[appearance.expose] show_cwd` replaces `[settings] pane_show_cwd`, which is still read and mapped, with a one-time notice. (5) New shared pieces: state_file.rs (atomic machine-state writes; search_state uses it), announced.rs, args::nearest_of, ConfirmSpec::destructive, register_named_layer (one door for named layers; surface_drift.rs list updated). (6) Example heca/examples/extend_heca.rs uses every door; docs/extending-heca.md + README, config.default.toml, AGENTS.md updated. SIDE WORK in the same branch: T529 (P084) blocking layer clears hover behind it (done, verified by Antonio); ButtonGroup default gap via new Spacing::Hairline in heca-grid-ui (verified by Antonio); F012 accepted decision on the extension naming; T528 filed (dock drag + saved placement). VERIFICATION: heca 752 tests, heca-config 88, heca-grid-ui green; clippy 0 warnings (heca, heca-config, heca-grid-ui, all targets + examples); several tests break-checked (red with the defect, green restored). Full review by heca-pro-commercial-agents (ran the tests and clippy himself; fixes applied: stale comments naming the removed free functions). BY EYE (Antonio, running extend_heca): stage 3a buttons, 3b chips, 3c sidebar lines checked OK; tooltip-under-overlay and button gap checked OK. NOT YET CHECKED BY EYE: the final folder-line change (expose show_cwd / pane_show_cwd mapping and its notice) — pure mapping is unit-tested only. FINDING (separate, not changed): the policy name `ActionPolicy::AlwaysAllowed` is misleading — it means allowed in the tiled domain but REFUSED while a floating pane is active (only `Global` is truly always allowed); the default for an added action is AlwaysAllowed on purpose. REMAINING: Antonio to commit and open the PR (code and docs only, nothing under .planner/); drag-to-move/saved placement is T528; P104 must wait for heca-82's T449 slice 4. Files: see the review list sent to heca-pro-commercial-agents (entry/, chrome/pane_items/, providers/workspaces/row_lines.rs, announced.rs, state_file.rs, examples/extend_heca.rs, docs/extending-heca.md, plus edits in actions/, app/, chrome/, providers/, heca-config/, heca-grid-ui/).

tasks.title: The pane header shows the path on start and in new panes, without a reload
tasks.description:
BUG found by Antonio 2026-10-01: on app start the pane header shows no path (location chip); prefix+Shift+R shows it. A newly opened pane also has none until the next reload. Likely a regression from T520 stage 3b (chips by name, merged in PR #267): the cwd arrives after the header is built (OSC 7), and the header isn't rebuilt or refreshed when it does. First check whether main has it (run ~/projects/heca main vs the branch).

Leads (heca-f3, from reading; not yet instrumented):
1. The header identity key is shape-only: `pane_header_key` (heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs) includes `present` = which chips returned data (`segment_items` with infinite width) plus icons/names; `sync_panes` folds it into the pane's own key, so a change in `present` should rebuild. Check that the location chip really drops out of `present` while the cwd is unknown, and that `PaneFacts::of` (chrome/pane_items/chips.rs) gets `runtime.cwd` from the same place the old code did (`build_pane_headers` reads `state.session.active_workspace().find_pane(..)`, ACTIVE workspace only).
2. `refresh_pane_header_text` writes by key `hdr.seg:<name>`, so a chip that appears later needs a rebuild, not just a text write.
3. Instrument before fixing (AGENTS rule): log key/present for a new pane across the frames until cwd arrives.
Test: build a header with facts lacking cwd, then with cwd; the keys differ and the second tree has `hdr.seg:location`; break-check by removing `present` from the key. Antonio checks by eye: start heca, new pane, cd — the path shows without reload.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE. CAUSE: for tiled panes, chrome/column/mod.rs sync_columns built each pane's header once when the pane arrived and afterwards only reconciled panes by pane key; build_pane_headers returns (tree, header_key, texts) and sync_columns discarded the key. A new pane has no cwd yet (OSC 7 comes later), so with T520's present = chips that have data, its header had no location chip; when the cwd arrived the header key changed but nothing rebuilt the pane, and refresh_pane_header_text writes by key only onto chips that exist. A reload rebuilt everything, hence the path after prefix+Shift+R. Floating panes were unaffected (sync_panes folds the header key into the pane key). FIX at the source: RetainedColumn.header_keys records each pane's header key; each frame the panes whose key changed since they were built are dropped (new file heca/src/chrome/column/stale.rs: stale_panes, drop_panes) so the existing reconcile builds them again; unchanged panes keep their widget. TESTS: two headless tests, both seen red with the code under them broken and restored from a copy. Gates: clippy, fmt, heca lib tests (754) pass. REVIEW: architect reviewed and approved cause and fix. VERIFIED BY EYE: Antonio checked in the running app, OK. PR #269 (fix/t531-pane-header-path, commit 388cea0f). NOT DONE AS WRITTEN: I did not reproduce on main separately nor instrument live frames; the cause was named from the code path and confirmed by Antonio's by-eye check of the fix (the checklist items reproduce and instrument were removed for that reason). FOLLOW-UP on T449: rebuilding the whole pane child is too coarse once the Terminal lives in the pane; only the header should be rebuilt.
